expect: Web Scraper's own infinite-scroll fixture. The LISTING page, not the category index: a first batch of phones is in the HTML and the rest are appended over AJAX as the viewport reaches the bottom, with no pager link.
evidence: Replaces https://webscraper.io/test-sites/e-commerce/scroll, which is the category INDEX of the same fixture and has no scroll behaviour at all: measured 2026-07-27 in CamoFox, document height 1348px unchanged over 6 scroll rounds, 6 images all decoded before scrolling, 0 load-more control, 0 pager links, and the render probe scored -81 chars. This URL is the listing the index links to. HTTP 200, 21,774 bytes, 3 , 0 rel="next", 0 paged . Render probe, 2 consecutive runs: images 6 -> 12, nodes 289 -> 397, height 1150 -> 1772px, text 784 -> 1,022 chars. Verdict pass 2/2 (+6 images).

HTTP 200, 1,644,025 bytes, 122 , loading="lazy" x108, the literal string 'infinite-scroll' x13. Verdict pass 2/2 (+19,535 and +23,049 chars). Note: the page also emits 1 rel="next" for SEO; the appended batches measured above are not reachable through it.

evidence: Replaces https://www.papermag.com/, whose infinite feed is gone. The old row's proof was the string '.infinite-scroll-wrapper' in the raw HTML, but measured 2026-07-27 in CamoFox the RENDERED document contains 0 elements matching [class*=infinite]/[class*=sentinel]/[class*=load-more], height is 4,436px unchanged over 6 scroll rounds, all 117 images are already decoded before scrolling (0 loading="lazy", 0 data-src), and there is no load-more control and no pager link - nothing is left to recover. expect: The Drupal gd_infinite_scroll feed the old row was aiming at, on the page that actually mounts it: the story list appends further batches from its load-more control, with no pager.
evidence: Replaces https://www.arabnews.com/, which is the front page and does not mount the feed. The old row's proof was that the raw HTML loads gd_infinite_scroll.js with {"items_selector":".objects-list .object-item","load_more":1}, but that config ships site-wide; measured 2026-07-27 in CamoFox the rendered FRONT PAGE has 0 elements matching [class*=infinite]/[class*=load-more], 0 load-more control, all 80 images decoded before scrolling, and document height 7,040 -> 7,040px (one run 7,040 -> 7,016, i.e. it SHRANK) with nodes and items identical - 3 runs, chars -8. This section page mounts the same module and it works. Render probe: images 26 -> 65, nodes 1,561 -> 2,392, height 3,732 -> 12,138px, text 6,589 -> 11,189 chars (+4,600). Sibling /media behaves identically (images 26 -> 62, height 3,762 -> 10,161px). NOTE: the control is a <span>/<div> whose handler is bound with addEventListener, so it is reachable only with the widened _LOADMORE_JS selector in the patch report - with the shipped 'button,a,[role=button],[onclick]' selector this row still fails.

expect: Story-card images are deferred and the card list itself extends on scroll, so the page moves four independent signals rather than only the decoded-image count.
evidence: Replaces https://www.mit.edu/, which cannot demonstrate the category because its ceiling is below the scoring floor: that page has 7 in total, of which 3 are decoded on load, so the largest possible gain is +4 against an images floor of 5, and measured 2026-07-27 it hits exactly that ceiling (3 -> 7 decoded, 5/5 runs) while nodes, items, height and chars are all unchanged. Lazy loading demonstrably works there; the page is simply too small to prove it. This row was chosen for margin: render probe, 2 consecutive runs, identical both times - images 16 -> 97, nodes 1,251 -> 2,205, height 3,995 -> 14,629px, text 7,037 -> 19,138 chars (+12,101). Passing on chars and pixels as well as images means it does not depend on images finishing their decode inside the probe's settle window, which is what makes the small-image rows flaky.

expect: Nearly the whole image set is deferred: the lead renders, the remaining 90-odd images decode only as the page is scrolled.
evidence: Replaces https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lazy_loading, which is an encyclopedia ARTICLE about the technique rather than a page that exercises it, and whose ceiling is likewise below the floor: 6 in total, 2 of them loading="lazy", 4 decoded on load, so the largest possible gain is +2 against a floor of 5 - measured 4 -> 6 decoded on 4/4 runs 2026-07-27, with nodes, items and height unchanged. HTTP 200, 878,914 bytes, 93 , loading="lazy" x91. Render probe, 2 consecutive runs: images 8 -> 145 both times. Verdict pass 2/2 (+137 images).

expect: Artwork rail images are placeholders until intersection; the decoded-image count multiplies once the viewport moves.
evidence: Replaces https://torquemag.io/, which no longer defers anything by the time the render tier measures it: measured 2026-07-27 in CamoFox, all 55 images are already decoded before any scrolling (0 loading="lazy" remaining in the rendered DOM), height 7,792px unchanged, so the ceiling for 'scrolling recovers content' is exactly 0. Its 55 data-src attributes are what the shipped _LAZY_RESOLVE_JS then re-points, which DROPS the decoded count to 39-46 (see the absolute-URL bug in the patch report). HTTP 200, 300,493 bytes, 18 , loading="lazy" x16. Render probe, 2 consecutive runs: images 6 -> 62 both times, nodes 1,926 -> 2,118, text 7,219 -> 7,907 chars. Verdict pass 2/2 (+56 images).
